Context
The Academy dashboard has a "Library" nav item already visible in the sidebar (academy.pursuearete.com/dashboard/library). It currently either routes to a blank page or a stub. This prompt implements the Library as a curated, per-course reading list with links to external papers and resources.
The Library is read-only — no user content, no uploads, no authentication beyond the existing session. It is a curated reference page maintained by the admin.
Part 1 — Library Data File
Create `academy/web/src/data/library.ts`.
This file exports the full reading list for all Academy courses. Structure:

```typescript
export interface LibraryItem {
  id: string;                     // unique slug, e.g. 'bobzien-sequent-2019'
  title: string;                  // full citation title
  author: string;                 // last name, first initial — e.g. 'Bobzien, S.'
  year: number;
  type: 'paper' | 'book' | 'reference' | 'encyclopedia';
  accessType: 'open-access' | 'library-access';
                                  // open-access: free direct link
                                  // library-access: requires university library or purchase
  url: string;                    // open-access: direct link; library-access: publisher record or PhilPapers entry
  urlLabel: string;               // short label for the link button, e.g. 'PhilArchive', 'SEP', 'OUP'
  description: string;            // 1–2 sentence annotation
  courses: string[];              // course IDs this applies to, e.g. ['phil-705']
  sessions: number[];             // session numbers within the course (empty = whole course)
  difficulty: 'introductory' | 'intermediate' | 'advanced';
  tags: string[];                 // e.g. ['conditionals', 'proof theory', 'lekton']
  libraryNote?: string;           // optional note for library-access items — alternative access route
}

export interface CourseLibrary {
  courseId: string;
  courseTitle: string;
  items: LibraryItem[];
}

```

Export helper functions:

```typescript
export function getLibraryForCourse(courseId: string): LibraryItem[] {
  return LIBRARY_ITEMS.filter(item => item.courses.includes(courseId));
}

export function getLibraryForSession(courseId: string, sessionNumber: number): LibraryItem[] {
  return LIBRARY_ITEMS.filter(item =>
    item.courses.includes(courseId) &&
    (item.sessions.length === 0 || item.sessions.includes(sessionNumber))
  );
}

export function getLibraryByTag(tag: string): LibraryItem[] {
  return LIBRARY_ITEMS.filter(item => item.tags.includes(tag.toLowerCase()));
}

```

Part 2 — Library Page
Create or replace `academy/web/src/app/dashboard/library/page.tsx`.
Design requirements

* Match the existing Academy dark theme (navy background, gold accents, DM Mono for labels)
* Three-column layout on desktop: left sidebar (course filter), main content (library items), right panel (tags/search)
* Mobile: stacked single column
* No authentication required beyond existing session
Layout
Left sidebar — Course filter:

* "All Courses" (default, shows everything)
* Per-course filter buttons: PHIL 701, PHIL 702, PHIL 703, PHIL 704, PHIL 705, GREK 101, LATN 101
* Active filter highlighted in gold
Main content — Library items: Group items by course when "All Courses" is selected. Within each course group, sort by session number (whole-course items first, then ascending session number).
Each library item card:

```
[TYPE BADGE]  [OPEN ACCESS | LIBRARY ACCESS badge]  [DIFFICULTY badge]
Author, Year
Title
Description
Tags: tag1 · tag2 · tag3
[Open →] (open-access) OR [Find in Library →] (library-access)
libraryNote — muted text, smaller font, if present

```

Badge colors:

* Type (PAPER / BOOK / ENCYCLOPEDIA / REFERENCE): DM Mono small pill, gold border
* `open-access`: small green pill — "Open Access"
* `library-access`: small amber pill — "Library Access"
* Difficulty: green (introductory), gold (intermediate), amber/orange (advanced)
The "Find in Library →" button for library-access items should open the url in a new tab and be styled slightly differently from the "Open →" button — e.g. outlined rather than filled — to visually signal it leads to a publisher page rather than a free PDF.
Right panel — Search and tags:

* Simple text search filtering item title, author, description, tags
* Tag cloud: all unique tags as clickable pills, clicking filters to items with that tag
* Access type filter: "All", "Open Access Only", "All including Library Access"
* "Clear filters" button
Session context widget
If the user is currently viewing a course session (detect from URL or session context), show a "Recommended for this session" callout at the top of the Library page listing the items tagged for that session. If not on a session page, omit this callout.

```
git add -A && git commit -m "Library: add data file with full reading list and accessType field"
git add -A && git commit -m "Library: implement library page with course filter, access badges, tag search"

```

Notes

* PowerShell on Windows — no `&&` chaining
* All open-access URLs are verified — do not modify or shorten them
* Library-access items: link to publisher record or PhilPapers entry — never to paywalled download pages. The user finds it through their institution from there.
* No PDF hosting — all items link to external repositories or publishers
* Admin only for adding items — the library data is a static file; no user-facing add/edit UI
* Do not touch PHIL 701 course content — the Pre-Seminar Briefing change is additive only
